title: Legacy SSH remote MacBookPro fails 'Host key verification failed' (exit 255) after its host changed to the .local hostname
outcome: When a legacy SSH remote's host is changed (for example to a hostname), host-key trust either carries over safely for the same verified key, or TermAl reports a typed 'unknown host key for <host>' diagnosis with the exact remediation. It never reports an opaque 502 RemoteConnectionUnavailable, and host-key checking is never weakened.
acceptance: A cause note with evidence shows, for the 2026-10-29 occurrence, whether the failing host-key check was an unknown-host entry for the new hostname or a real key mismatch, comparing stored and live key fingerprints without changing trust.

TermAl reports a host-key verification failure on a legacy SSH remote as a typed diagnosis naming the host, the alias and the presented key fingerprint, plus the one safe remediation, instead of only 502 RemoteConnectionUnavailable; covered by a deterministic test.

Changing a legacy remote's host to a name whose presented key equals an already trusted key for that remote does not silently fail; it is either carried over safely under existing pin rules or surfaced as above; no path weakens StrictHostKeyChecking.
